evidence.quote: the as-cast high Nb-TiAl alloy ingot was subjected to hot-isostatic pressing at 1,300 °C and 120 MPa for 3 h under argon atmosphere with the following furnace cooling, and a homogenizing annealing process was performed at 1,250 °C for 6 h after HIP.

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure
evidence.quote: the alloy samples after HIP and annealing were heated at temperatures of 1,400 °C, 1,340 °C and 1,250 °C for 30 min, respectively, followed by water quenching or furnace cooling.

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure
evidence.quote: When the alloy is quenched at 1,340 °C, the white β/B2 phases disappear completely and the microstructure is composed of α phase.

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure
evidence.quote: When the quenching temperature is reduced to 1,250 °C, a lot of black acicular γ phases appear and γ/α2 colonies form in the microstructure.

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure
evidence.quote: When the alloy is heated at 1,400 °C (α+β phases region), a full lamellar (FL) structure of γ/α2 lamellar is obtained after furnace cooling (Fig. 6a).

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure
evidence.quote: The microstructure of the alloy heat treated at 1,340 °C (α single phase region) is similar to that heat treated at 1,400 °C, but the size of lamellar colonies is refined.

There are a few β/B2 phase and equiaxed γ phase grains at the lamellar boundary in both air cooled and furnace cooled samples, indicating that recrystallization occurs during the forging and cooling processes.
